text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- SAO PAULO HAS RECORD LOSS WITH CARGO ROBBERY

Sao Paulo transportation firms have lost 95 million reais to cargo robbery so far this year. Losses in 1996 are likely to be 15 percent higher than in 1995, according to Sao Paulo Transportation Firms Union.
-- ELETROPAULO SHOWS NET IN THIRD QUARTER

Sao Paulo power utility Eletropaulo is recovering from its huge losses in 1995. The company showed a 68.556 million real net profit in the third quarter, seven times higher than its first half's earnings.
-- BANESPA SHOWS 786 MLN REAL NET

Sao Paulo state bank Banespa reported a net profit of 786.3 million reais in the first nine months. Banespa's figures were included in a report sent by the bank's administrative council to Sao Paulo Finance Secretary Yoshiaki Nakano and Central Bank director Alkimar Moura.
-- PUBLIC SECTOR DEFICIT FALLS WITH GDP CORRECTION
The public sector deficit compared with gross domestic product fell in September after the Central Bank decided to use 1995 GDP figures updated by the National Statistics Institute (IBGE).
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- ONE BLN PEOPLE UNEMPLOYED
One billion people, or nearly a third of the global workforce, are out of a job or under-employed, said a report by the International Labour Organisation (ILO).
-- COVAS SAYS SEALED DEBT REFINANCING ACCORD

Sao Paulo state this week will sign a debt refinancing deal with the federal government, said Sao Paulo state governor Mario Covas. Under the plan, 20 percent of Sao Paulo's 43 billion real debt will have to be paid through asset sales and 80 percent will be refinanced for 30 years.
-- MURDERER OF CHICO MENDES ARRESTED IN PARANA STATE
The Federal Police recaptured Darci Alves Pereira, son of Darly Alves, convicted murderer of Amazon rubber-tapper leader Chico Mendes, in Guaira, in the southern state of Parana.
O GLOBO
-- FERNANDO HENRIQUE UNITES PMDB AGAINST MALUF
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso united the Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMDB) against Sao Paulo mayor Paulo Maluf.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo Newsroom, 55-11-2485412
